name: EARQUAKE – Wolfgang Voigt 1991 – 1999
editorial_article:
"EARQUAKE – Wolfgang Voigt 1991 – 1999" is a comprehensive, monumental retrospective box set released by the Cologne-based label Kompakt in 2019. It serves as an exhaustive chronicle of the solo musical output of Wolfgang Voigt, a seminal figure in German electronic music, during the 1990s. The project, which was available exclusively through the label's online platform, gathered nearly every solo piece Voigt produced under his sprawling network of aliases during that decade, totaling 303 individual tracks, 75 of which were previously unreleased. It also included the previously unreleased 1995 album, *Mit Maschinen Sprechen*.

The collection stands as a testament to Voigt’s relentless creative energy and his role in defining the sound of 90s techno. Moving through phases of hardcore acid, gabber, and dadaist experiments, the tracks on "EARQUAKE" demonstrate his mastery of the sampler, which he used as a tool for "quotation-pop-art-expressionism." By sampling everything from Schlager and Polka to classical music and jazz, Voigt deconstructed and reconstituted the sounds of popular culture into a continuous, techno-informed digital landscape. This monumental retrospective spans his work under various projects like Mike Ink, Love Inc., M:I:5, Wassermann, Studio 1, and Freiland, mapping a decade characterized by both minimalist discourse and maximalist experimentation. The project notably excludes his ambient work as GAS and other collaborations, focusing instead on his solo, techno-centric explorations that defined the ethos of the early Kompakt era and its precursor, Profan. As a career-spanning survey, it offers a bird's-eye view of a visionary producer who helped steer the development of minimalist and abstract techno in Germany.
editorial_pitch: A massive, 303-track digital retrospective documenting the entire solo output of electronic music pioneer Wolfgang Voigt during the 1990s, capturing the chaotic, transformative evolution of German techno through his various influential aliases.
